== Book 4 ==

== Biography ==

Jim is a horse who pulls the buggy driven by Zeb, described by Zeb as an animal who "knows his business," though on the road to Hugson's Ranch he shows a stubborn streak, refusing to move until struck with the whip.

When invisible bears attack in the Valley of Voe, a magic leaf is rubbed on each of Jim's hoofs and on the buggy's tires, letting him walk on the surface of a river; he frees himself from his unseen attackers with a few kicks and escapes across the water, though not before deep gashes appear on his flanks.

Jim's Kentucky breeding is noted when he pounds along at a great rate despite an ungraceful gait. He loses a race against the Sawhorse, arriving panting at the canopy well after the wooden horse has already returned to cheers from the Ozites; the chapter that follows is one in which the Hungry Tiger teaches Jim a lesson.

According to the chapter orientation notes, Jim falls together with Dorothy, Zeb, and the buggy through a crack opened by an earthquake, landing in the glass city of the Mangaboos, where he and the kitten Eureka unexpectedly gain the power of speech.

== Narrative role ==

Jim is introduced as the horse pulling the buggy in which Zeb drives Dorothy from Hugson's Siding toward Hugson's Ranch, after Dorothy arrives there by train and meets Zeb. Shortly after, an earthquake splits the ground beneath them, and Jim falls with Dorothy, Zeb, and the buggy into a great crack leading deep underground. They land in the glass city of the Mangaboos, a vegetable people ruled by a Prince, where Jim unexpectedly gains the power of speech alongside the kitten Eureka. When the Mangaboos' new Princess later passes judgment on the group, she spares Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard but condemns Jim, along with Eureka and the piglets, to be driven into the Black Pit within the mountain. Jim, Dorothy, Zeb, Eureka, and the Wizard subsequently escape a group of invisible bears in the Valley of Voe by rubbing magic leaves onto their feet so they can walk on water. Once in Oz, Jim takes part in a reunion with Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, and the Woggle-Bug, an occasion that ends with a race between Jim and the Sawhorse. Jim loses that race and, in anger, kicks the Sawhorse hard enough to break its leg and ear, which prompts the Hungry Tiger to tackle him in response. Afterward, as Dorothy and Zeb bid farewell to Oz, Dorothy returns to Kansas while Zeb and Jim make their way back to Hugson's Ranch.

== Personality ==

Jim's early behavior marks him as stubborn: when urged onward at night he needed a shaken rein, a crack of the whip, and a touch to the flanks before he would move, answering with "a low moan of protest" rather than open refusal — reluctant compliance rather than defiance. Zeb's confidence in him ("Jim knows his business all right") suggests the horse is otherwise dependable once in motion.

That same underlying reliability surfaces under real danger: attacked by unseen assailants in the Valley of Voe, Jim frees himself with a few sharp kicks and obeys the Wizard's shouted order to run for the river without hesitation, suggesting an instinct for self-preservation paired with responsiveness to command in a crisis. His effort in the race against the Sawhorse — running hard despite lacking grace, "to do credit to his Kentucky breeding" — points to a competitive pride bound up with his lineage.

== Appearance ==

Jim is a horse of Kentucky breeding, a lineage reflected in his running style even though he does not look graceful while doing it. He has a long nose — patted by Zeb to calm him — and a big, boney build, with big hoofs that pound the ground at a great rate when he runs.

Eureka is noted nestling comfortably beside his big, boney body, underscoring his large frame relative to a small kitten.

== Powers ==

In the glass city of the Mangaboos, Jim unexpectedly gains the power of speech, a trait ordinary horses do not possess.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Zeb]]''' — acquaintance. Zeb is the one who unties, drives, and urges Jim throughout the journey, at one point coaxing him with "Jim knows his business all right—don't you, Jim?" while patting his nose; when Jim proves stubborn Zeb turns to the whip, after which Jim advances "with a low moan of protest." The bond between them seems to be one of routine familiarity between driver and horse rather than close companionship.

'''[[Sawhorse]]''' — friendly_rivalry. Racing the Sawhorse toward Ozma's canopy, Jim's "big hoofs pounded away at a great rate" in a manner said to do credit to his Kentucky breeding, yet the wooden Sawhorse proved "swifter than the wind" and reached the finish long before Jim came "panting up." The contest appears to have soured into real hostility, as Jim reportedly lashed out at the Sawhorse afterward — an episode remembered as the moment "the Hungry Tiger teaches Jim a lesson."

'''[[DOROTHY]]''' — friend. Dorothy rides in the buggy Jim pulls, including across the river in the Valley of Voe, where the horse carried the party safely once the magic leaves let him walk on the water's surface. Her question "Can your horse talk?" suggests a link to Jim's unexpected gain of speech, hinting at a bond of curiosity and trust rather than mere transport.

'''[[Eureka]]''' — friend. The kitten Eureka is described nestling "comfortably beside his big, boney body," a detail that could indicate an easy companionship between the two animals who, according to accounts of their descent into the underground realm, both unexpectedly gained the power of speech there.

'''[[WIZARD]]''' — ally. The Wizard directs Jim at critical moments, shouting "Run for the river!" so that the horse could free himself from unseen tormentors, and earlier rubbed the magic leaf upon Jim's hoofs to let him cross the water safely. Their interactions suggest the Wizard acts as a guide and protector to Jim rather than a mere companion in the buggy.

== Trivia ==

* Despite an ungainly gait, Jim's speed is credited to his Kentucky breeding.
* He is referred to as "the cab-horse," a term used to contrast him with the smaller, wooden Sawhorse.

=== Events ===

* Dorothy Gale arrives by train at Hugson's Siding and meets Zeb, who drives her toward Hugson's Ranch in a buggy pulled by the horse Jim.
* An earthquake splits the earth beneath them, and Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and the buggy fall into a great crack leading deep underground.
* They land in the glass city of the Mangaboos, a vegetable people ruled by a Prince, where Jim and the kitten Eureka unexpectedly gain the power of speech.
* The new Princess spares Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard but condemns Jim, Eureka, and the piglets to be driven into the Black Pit in the mountain.
* Wizard, Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka escape invisible bears in the Valley of Voe by rubbing magic leaves on their feet to walk on water.
* In Oz they reunite with the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, and the Woggle-Bug, ending with a race between Jim and the Sawhorse.
* Jim loses race against Sawhorse and kicks it in anger, breaking its leg and ear; Hungry Tiger tackles Jim in response.
* Dorothy and Zeb say farewell to Oz; Dorothy returns to Kansas and Zeb and Jim return to Hugson's Ranch.
